note: SHRINK-ONLY, and every row carries a DECISION. Task 67 measured 151 ceiling violations tree-wide and owned every one of them to itself; task 99 adjudicated them. A row is either an EXEMPTION -- permanent, naming the invariant its count encodes, with no owner because there is no work to own -- or a PAYDOWN work order naming the concrete seam that removes it. There is no third state: `owner` is refused by the schema, so a row can never again sit here pointing at a task that has closed. A violation worse than its declared value, or at a location with no row, fails the gate; so does a row the tree no longer produces, so the file only shrinks. `ratchet.max_rows` must equal the row count and `ratchet.max_paydown_rows` may only fall, both pinned by value in tests/gates/test_module_ceilings.py. NO file_over_cap row is accepted under scripts/agentware_lib/ (task 21 satisfied that cap outright), and no row may sit inside a package task 21 round 1 split. When the last row goes, the gate is simply green.

groups.reason: ADJUDICATED PERMANENT (task 99). Each row's count is a property of the code rather than neglect: the branches are a closed taxonomy, a report-every-problem check set, or a per-field coercion of an untrusted external schema, and collapsing any pair of them is the defect the structure exists to prevent. The `invariant` on each row says which of those it is, in terms a reader can check against the body. These rows have no owner because there is no work to own -- but they are still CEILINGS: the declared value is the worst the location may be, and a location that improves must have its row lowered or removed in the same change.

rows.invariant: Its branches ARE the ordered checkpoints of one git merge transaction: each turns a distinct failure (not-an-ancestor, checkout, refused merge, prose conflict, rebuild, nothing-lost gate, commit) into `merge --abort` plus one named status from the closed set {merged, skipped, prose-conflict, error}, so no path can fall through to commit and silently drop a lane's KB work.

Its branches are the abort arms of a fixed serial merge-queue stage order (package, then KB, then gates, then artifact commit), and each arm is the SOLE producer of one member of the closed status vocabulary the disposition reader consumes, so collapsing any two loses which stage aborted the integration. The whole body is thirty-eight lines against a cap of twelve branches.

It reports EVERY manifest defect rather than the first: each branch appends one error string naming its offender to an ordered list and continues, so the branch count IS the check count across schema, name, concurrency range, node and edge shape, checkpoint vocabulary, plan existence, self-extension implies manual, dangling and duplicate edges, and cycles.

Same report-all-checks property at line granularity: the length is linear in the check count because each check is one condition plus its offender-naming message literal, so 124 lines is the message text of about twenty checks and not extra logic. Splitting would fragment one ordered defect report across files to remove a four-line overage.

Its branches are the arms of a total verdict taxonomy: each maps one (plan state, terminal outcome, lane or merged, claim age) case onto exactly one (status, disposition, detail) triple and returns immediately, with an unknown plan state and an unknown outcome both defaulting to HALT. Collapsing a pair is the bug: done-and-merged, done-with-no-lane and done-awaiting-merge are three scheduler actions.

Same taxonomy at line granularity: the body is a decision table whose length is linear in its case count, each arm a short assignment block over one accumulator plus its return, with the comments recording which observed failure each arm exists to prevent. No arm shares mutable state with another, so splitting the table spans the fail-closed default across files without removing a case.

Its branches are the cells of a TOTAL transition matrix over recorded status in {absent, installed, quarantined, blocked, unknown} by whether the vetter blocks by whether the tree hash still matches the approved one, each cell writing one lockfile status and bumping one counter, with the trailing arm re-adjudicating an unknown status so no cell falls through. Collapsing a pair breaks a stated rule: a blocked skill must not be re-prompted, and an installed one still owes its cache-integrity check.

Every branch coerces exactly one field of an untrusted `gh issue list --json` export (item shape, the url/number/index reference chain, title, body, labels[].name) into either a total value or a REPORTED rejection, so the count is the external schema's optional-field count and dropping one either crashes on a malformed export or drops an issue in silence.

It appends to an errors list and never returns early, so it reports EVERY violation of its three documented FAIL conditions (a leak, a malformed or missing ledger, a count mismatch) across every entry and every staged proposal: the branch count IS the check count plus the isinstance guards that let it survive a corrupt index instead of crashing on one.

Each branch admits exactly one SPELLING by which a promotion can clear an R-SI-03 marker (indexed skills-category id, indexed skills-proposed path id, its proposal-<slug> alias, an on-disk proposal slug, an on-disk skills/<name>/SKILL.md), so the count is the size of that closed alias set and dropping an arm re-opens the recorded bug where a finished run was killed by `worklog scan`.

Every branch is one field-level coercion of an untrusted metrics.jsonl line into the per-iteration record: the event-type discriminator, the `isinstance(it, int) and not bool` exclusion without which True fabricates iteration 1, the phase/stage/main fallback chain, the float() guard on wall time and the last-non-None-wins folds. Dropping one lets a malformed event invent or corrupt an iteration.

Nine branches are one `getattr(args, field, None) or default` per key of the committed terminal-event schema, which makes every emitted sink line TOTAL so no reader has to special-case a null; the rest are the never-block-the-loop degradations R-ORG-06 requires, so a terminal event is still emitted, or cleanly skipped, on every failure exit path.

Every branch either selects one arm of the closed session-identity taxonomy (kind in {loop, plan, work} by confidence in {high, provisional, pending} by terminal in {complete, ended, incomplete}) or coerces one untrusted row field into that closed set, and the ARM ORDER is the semantics, so collapsing any pair merges two identities the contract declares distinct.

It is a TOTAL parse of an untrusted `check:` string into a CLOSED kind set: every branch is one kind of the grammar or one arity/domain constraint of that kind, and every return path lands on a declared kind or on one of the three sentinels, so nothing can fall through to a runnable kind. That totality is what stops an unparseable premise silently grounding the R-GND-01 gate.

Every branch coerces one attacker-influenceable reviewer-output field into a closed set and RECORDS the coercion as a schema error rather than dropping it (required-field presence, dimension against the declared keys, severity fail-closed to high, verdict casefold), so the count is the field-by-closed-set count and removing one lets an off-enum token reach the blocking decision.

It returns exactly one of three closed classes (url:, cmd:, path:) and every branch is one documented discrimination or volatility-masking rule of that taxonomy: the userinfo strip, tool-kind-is-authoritative, sigil-beats-space, the trailing-extension tiebreak, the numeric rotation peel. Collapsing a pair either leaks a credential fragment into a persistent ledger or mints an unbounded key class.

Every branch is either a shape coercion of one untrusted field of the hand-editable registry.json into a closed set or the emission of one of the three O5 error classes, and it reports EVERY bad row rather than the first, so it can never early-return past a branch. The whole body is eighteen lines: splitting it yields two eight-line halves and a four-line parent.

Every boolean operand is one arm of the five-part ACR win gate and has a matching `passed` entry in the returned checks dict, so the branch count IS the number of independently reported gate conditions and collapsing any operand silently deletes a reported check while leaving the verdict looking equally well evidenced.

The branches are the complete redaction ladder for a path that must never reach the committed public ledger absolute or operator-identifying (R-LOC-03): each is one rung (already relative, knowledge-dir relative, HOME relative, basename) or that rung's validity test, so no path through the function can return an absolute or identity-bearing string. The body is thirty-nine lines.

Its branches are the closed arms of the org recall-scoping table (flat corpus with no facet, shared only, all teams, the shared pseudo-team, a named team, and the default of the caller's own shard unioned with shared skills), each returning a DIFFERENT corpus and each returning immediately, so collapsing any pair IS the cross-shard leak R-ORG-02 forbids.

Each arm maps exactly one member of the codex `item.completed` type vocabulary, which the upstream CLI owns and this package does not, onto the sinks' fixed (tool, input, response, status) tuple, coercing an untrusted exit code into the closed set {ok, ERR}. The count tracks the upstream type set, and a same-file helper extraction would additionally drop the body under its recorded floor.

Its arms ARE the Claude transcript content-block vocabulary (bare string, text, thinking, tool_use, tool_result), a schema this package does not own, each isinstance-coercing an untrusted block into the renderer's closed line vocabulary. One arm per schema member across a twenty-seven-line body: the count tracks the upstream block set, so it moves when that set does and not otherwise.

The file defines ZERO functions: every line is the adjudication row table, one row per adjudicated body divergence carrying host, floor and absorbers plus the hand-written rationale a reviewer needs beside its row. Its length measures the adjudicated-divergence count, not any procedure. The repo's own precedent for splitting it (the shim-retirement sibling) took a seam a SHARED adjudication reason already named; the residual rows each carry a reason of their own.

Its branches ARE the closed grammar of a constant string key: the three AST forms a key can take (subscript slice, `.get(k, default)` first argument, dict-literal key) each paired with the Constant-and-is-a-string narrowing the metric charges as an extra boolean operand. The contract pins that boundary deliberately, so a key held in a variable stays invisible.

It reports EVERY registry disagreement rather than the first (retired id, retired label, unknown ids, order mismatch, per-row label mismatch, missing-set mismatch), so its branches are exactly six independently appended problems plus the five comprehension filters that compute their operands, accumulating into one list with no early return past a check.

Twelve of its branches sit INSIDE the returned dict literal, one conditional expression or comprehension filter per DERIVED COLUMN of the fixed capture-row schema (namespace, side, direction, unset-means, default, read sites, write sites), so the count is the row schema's derived-column count and not control flow. The body is a single return.

It reports EVERY normalizer defect rather than the first (defined exactly once, layer-legal owner, string-element filtering, fresh-list construction, no raw-field return), so its branches are five independently appended errors plus the three walks and the isinstance narrowing that find them. Each message is a distinct documented failure mode.

Its branches ARE the quoting states of a shell tokenizer: one character loop and six mutually exclusive arms (backslash escape, single quote, double quote, brace open, brace close, comment start), whose boolean operands are exactly the state flags each arm must see cleared plus the word-boundary test. Any decomposition either threads the whole state tuple through helpers or loses the single-pass property.

Its branches are the closed taxonomy of markdown link kinds: three skip classes (empty or external, placeholder, exempted file) and four distinct problem details (unreadable file, no such anchor here, no such file, no such anchor in the target), each arm ending in a continue or one problem append. Hoisting the loop body leaves thirteen branches in the classifier, still over the cap.

It is ONE ordered go-live scenario in a single knowledge dir where each stage asserts against state the previous stage mutated: seed, first mine run, then a NEW session on a SECOND run suppressed only by the cross-run ledger, then drain, review, approve, capture, digest, then an idempotent re-run. Splitting it into methods would either re-seed (destroying the cross-RUN claim, which is the point) or make correctness depend on undefined method ordering. It carries six branches, not 153.
